incidents.victim: SonicWall SMA appliance customers (government, MSSPs, enterprises)
incidents.vector: Attackers chained two SonicWall Secure Mobile Access zero-days (CVE-2026-15409, a maximum-severity unauthenticated SSRF, and CVE-2026-15410) to gain root-level remote code execution on internet-facing appliances.
incidents.impact: A threat actor tied to the Inc ransomware-as-a-service group used the flaws to breach multiple enterprise networks, steal credentials and session data, pivot to domain controllers, and in at least one case deploy ransomware; some victims who patched saw attackers roll the appliance back to a vulnerable state to keep access.

incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — data extortion and SIM-swapping
incidents.vector: Two leading members of a young English-speaking cybercrime collective used social engineering and SIM-swap techniques to breach corporate networks, including the 2024 attack that froze Transport for London's systems.
incidents.impact: The UK's National Crime Agency secured 66-month sentences for the pair in Britain's largest-ever cybercrime prosecution; one was tied by US authorities to at least 120 attacks, extortion of 47 US organizations, and roughly $89.5 million in traced cryptocurrency.

incidents.vector: The FulcrumSec extortion group gained access via exposed or hardcoded credentials and unpatched applications, then used AI agents to analyze the stolen data and maximize negotiating leverage.
incidents.impact: The group claims to have stolen 1.3TB of data (700,000+ files) including five undisclosed drug programs, RNA delivery research, and private AI drug-discovery models, asserting the theft could save competitors years of development; initial ransom demand was $25 million.

incidents.vector: Attackers breached servers at Japan's largest refrigerated-logistics operator; the company disconnected key systems to contain the intrusion, and it remains unclear whether ransomware was involved.
incidents.impact: The outage halted frozen-food shipments across 140 distribution centers, leaving all 1,300+ KFC Japan restaurants short on ingredients and disrupting supermarket chains, sushi and bento operators; some affected servers held personal data still under investigation.

incidents.victim: Software users in the US and Europe
incidents.vector: A Russian-speaking actor (tracked as UAT-11795) used ClickFix-style social engineering to deliver trojanized installers for popular tools (MobaXterm, Zoom, WebEx, DBeaver, FACEIT), dropping a Python-based 'Starland RAT' and a PowerShell C2 implant.
incidents.impact: The malware harvests browser credentials and cryptocurrency wallet assets, establishes persistent C2 (with a Polygon smart-contract fallback), and can deploy follow-on payloads including CastleStealer and Remcos RAT; infections are concentrated in the United States.

incidents.vector: Threat actors are actively exploiting three SharePoint vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-32201, CVE-2026-45659, CVE-2026-56164) affecting all supported on-prem versions to gain remote code execution and steal IIS machine keys.
incidents.impact: CISA warned that successful exploitation enables unauthorized access, persistence via stolen machine keys, and malware deployment on internet-exposed SharePoint servers; all three CVEs are in CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.

incidents.victim: NATO/EU logistics routes and Ukrainian military
incidents.vector: Russian intelligence scanned the internet for exposed IP cameras and exploited weak or default credentials and outdated firmware, then used image-recognition software to automatically analyze the feeds.
incidents.impact: Dutch intelligence agencies (AIVD/MIVD) said hacked cameras were used to monitor NATO military transport routes and weapons shipments to Ukraine, and in some cases to locate Ukrainian troops for lethal targeting; compromised cameras were also found along Dutch logistics routes.

incidents.victim: Poland energy grid and water treatment facilities
incidents.vector: Russia's FSB signals-intelligence arm conducted cyber-sabotage operations against Polish energy and water infrastructure; investigators traced the intrusion infrastructure to an FSB-linked cluster.
incidents.impact: A December 2025 attack came 'very close' to causing a blackout that would have cut heating to half a million people; the UK and EU responded with their first joint cyber sanctions package, targeting 30+ individuals and entities across Russia's cyber ecosystem including Lumma Stealer operators.

incidents.vector: FSB Center 16 actors scan the internet for networking devices with weak or default SNMP community strings, then issue SNMP Set-Requests to copy device configurations and exfiltrate them via TFTP to actor-controlled servers, occasionally exploiting Cisco Smart Install and known CVEs.
incidents.impact: A joint advisory from the US and a dozen allied nations (NSA, CISA, FBI, ACSC and others) detailed a decade-plus campaign opportunistically compromising routers across communications, energy, financial services, government, and healthcare sectors for espionage.

incidents.vector: The Gentlemen ransomware-as-a-service program gains access via edge-device vulnerabilities (firewalls, VPNs), brute force, stolen credentials and initial access brokers, using custom Go/C encryptors, a Go backdoor, and an EDR-killer framework.
incidents.impact: Unit 42 reports the group claimed 580 victims across 77 countries since inception, with victims up roughly 6x in the first half of 2026 versus late 2025 (117 in June alone), making it the second-most-active RaaS program of the year; manufacturing is the most-targeted sector.

incidents.vector: A large-scale campaign scans websites and exploits numerous known CMS and plugin vulnerabilities (WordPress plugins, Craft CMS, Joomla, MetInfo and others) allowing unauthenticated file upload, RCE, SSRF or deserialization to deploy webshells.
incidents.impact: Australia's ACSC issued a critical alert warning that compromised web servers are being used for defacement, credential capture, malware distribution, and as pivots for broader network compromise, with many Australian small and medium businesses already impacted.

incidents.vector: A financially motivated ransomware group exploited a vulnerability in a system that had not been updated for two years and dwelled in Latvia's state forestry company's network for over a week before detection.
incidents.impact: The attack knocked out mapping, hunting and contractor systems and leaked ~44GB of stolen data (internal documents, source code, cryptographic keys, credentials); the same actor also compromised a server at pharmaceutical firm Olpha, though election infrastructure LVM helped build was confirmed unaffected.

incidents.victim: UK Foreign Office, British embassies, local councils
incidents.vector: Credentials for firewall and VPN servers were harvested during the earlier 'FortiBleed' campaign, in which an actor stole credentials from nearly 80,000 Fortinet devices.
incidents.impact: Stolen credentials for the UK Foreign Office, British embassies and some local councils are being sold as a single archive for $60,000 by a threat actor known as SantaAd, creating espionage and follow-on intrusion risk for sensitive government networks.

incidents.vector: Attackers exploited a vulnerability in third-party software used by an email platform KDDI operates for five Japanese internet service providers.
incidents.impact: The breach exposed more than 12.2 million customer email addresses and 7.6 million passwords; KDDI patched the flaw, said no other systems were compromised, and affected ISPs are forcing mandatory password resets.

incidents.vector: A China-nexus actor (tracked as UAT-7810) exploits known vulnerabilities in unpatched Ruckus wireless routers and other edge devices to deploy new custom malware families (LONGLEASH, DOGLEASH, JARLEASH) and build operational relay box networks.
incidents.impact: Cisco Talos reports the actor maintains and expands the 'LapDogs' ORB network — proxy infrastructure that secondary China-nexus espionage groups then use to obscure and launch attacks against high-value targets.

incidents.vector: A pro-Ukraine hacktivist group breached one of Russia's largest construction firms and gained broad access to its infrastructure over a period in May.
incidents.impact: The attackers claim to have wiped roughly 3,000 servers and workstations plus 700 virtual machines, deleted all backups, and exfiltrated more than 650TB of sensitive documents; the breach was disclosed only recently.
